title: Take staging and production dark
description:
Both answer unauthenticated requests from the open internet today. Neither needs to serve anyone before this initiative ships.

Done when: only development (and marketing apex) is reachable as a Chattic.us app; staging and production thin-turn/web app hosts refuse unauthenticated public use. Redeploy tracked under this dark-environments epic. Never cdk deploy --all. Do not destroy Computers/Snapshots. Marketing at chattic.us stays up.

comments.author: rap@endymion.com

comments.author: rap@endymion.com
comments.text:
## Questions for architects

Intent: dark **staging.chattic.us** and production **app/hey thin-turn+web**, keep **dev.chattic.us** and marketing **chattic.us / www**.

1. Confirm production **hey.chattic.us** (and leftover **app.chattic.us** if DNS still exists) should go dark, not the marketing CloudFront.
2. Preferred mechanism: CloudFront WAF allowlist, disable distributions, or remove public aliases? We will not steal apex/www from ChatticusMarketingWeb.
3. Is a 403/401 from the existing invoke-key check enough, or must unauthenticated TCP/HTTPS fail closed at the edge?
